VERSION COMPASS / FUTURE RELEASE PREPARATION
Prep for Splunk 11.x
Upcoming Enterprise 11.x+ · Discovery checked 2026-11-02
Independent public-source preparation guide. Not an official Cisco or Splunk publication.
No version-specific public 11.x release announcement was located in the targeted official-source searches on
November 2, 2026. This bounded discovery does not prove none exists. Release timing, deployment
requirements and migration paths remain unconfirmed here. Individual preparation claims retain their own
assessment dates below.
Screen selection: All preparation areas · All public updates. This report includes the complete public update
inventory, every preparation area, all open questions and numbered citations.
Public updates
An announcement records a stated plan. Released documentation, exact compatibility matrices and service-
specific evidence are required before a plan becomes an installation path, supported pairing or availability claim.
0 version-specific 11.x announcements recorded. Current-release context is labeled separately.
2026-09-30 · Published announcement · 10.6 context
Review custom version-detection logic
The 10.6 announcement asks app and automation owners to use supported product-identification methods
rather than relying on version numbers alone to distinguish Enterprise from Cloud.
Scope: This is published 10.6 guidance and a useful preparation task. It does not announce an 11.x release
or a migration path.
Claim verified 2026-11-02 · [7]
2026-09-15 · Published announcement · adjacent product scope
Kubernetes-based architecture announced for Cisco AI POD for Splunk
Cisco’s announcement describes Kubernetes-based self-managed AI infrastructure for Splunk customers. It
describes AI Assistant as available and Agent Launchpad as coming later in 2026.

Claim verified 2026-11-02 · [8]
Prepare now
These are editorial preparation actions supported by current documentation. They are not confirmed 11.x
requirements.
Current baseline · source discrepancy · SOK 3.2.0 / matrix Enterprise 10.0.12–10.6.0
Start with an exact Operator compatibility tuple
The 3.2 help matrix lists Kubernetes 1.32–1.37 and Enterprise 10.0.12–10.6.0. The linked change log lists
Kubernetes 1.32–1.36 and Enterprise 10.6.0 for 3.2.0. Its September 8 heading also differs from the matrix’s
September 24 release date.
Scope: Preserve both published scopes. Confirm the exact Kubernetes, Operator and Enterprise
combination before using it; neither source certifies 11.x.
Prepare now: Record the intended Kubernetes distribution and version, Operator release and exact Enterprise
build. Resolve the differing 3.2 version/date statements before relying on their disputed range.
Claim verified 2026-11-02 · [1] · [2]
Current preparation guidance · Current Operator validated architecture
Design storage and failure recovery before moving workloads
The Operator validated architecture describes single-site and multi-site layouts, persistent storage, SmartStore
and the App Framework. It discourages distributed non-clustered deployments because they lack the
redundancy expected in Kubernetes.
Scope: Current architecture guidance is preparation context. An 11.x topology, sizing or migration
requirement is not established.
Prepare now: Map search heads, indexers and management roles to availability zones, storage classes,
recovery objectives and a tested restore design.
Claim verified 2026-11-02 · [3]
Current preparation guidance · Current Operator App Framework and premium-app guidance

Inventory apps and configuration delivery
The current Operator architecture covers app distribution through the App Framework and separate
considerations for premium apps. Existing apps, add-ons, scripts, credentials and filesystem assumptions need
their own review.
Scope: App installation and a container image do not prove ES, ITSI, SOAR or third-party compatibility with
11.x.
Prepare now: Build an app and integration inventory, identify persistent state and external dependencies, and
plan repeatable deployment and rollback tests. Keep exact premium-product matrices as a separate decision
gate.
Claim verified 2026-11-02 · [3]
Current baseline · Enterprise 10.6 documentation; capability introduced in 10.4+
Recheck search resource controls
Enterprise 10.6 documentation describes Advanced mode with writable CPU and memory cgroup controllers and
the full categories, pools and placement/monitoring/admission rule set. Basic mode supports admission rules
only. Its allow_basic fallback setting is false by default; Kubernetes use requires explicitly enabling it.
Scope: Basic mode does not establish full workload-pool or placement-rule parity. This is current-release
behavior, not an 11.x promise.
Prepare now: Inventory admission, placement and monitoring rules; validate which controls work in the chosen
current lab topology before assuming equivalent behavior.
Claim verified 2026-11-03 · [4]
Review status: Exact Enterprise 10.6 source retrieved and its modes, activation and mode-status sections
assessed on November 3, 2026. The CLI reports basic/advanced; Basic does not load categories or pools.
Expected Advanced-mode preflight warnings are not proof that an intentional Basic deployment is
misconfigured.
Planning option · Current Splunk Cloud Platform migration guidance
Compare the future operating model with a Cloud migration
Splunk Lantern’s organizational-readiness guide calls for a Cloud migration staffing plan, a communications plan
and a post-migration staffing transition plan. It describes options for shifting duties toward business value,
platform optimization or other work after infrastructure responsibilities change.
Scope: Cloud is a separate migration program. Enterprise announcements do not establish Cloud rollout,
entitlement or FedRAMP Moderate/High authorization.

Still to be confirmed
When will 11.x be available, and at what release stage?
A confirmed public release date, preview or general-availability stage is not recorded in this evidence set.
Evidence to watch: A dated official announcement and version-specific release notes.
What deployment models will 11.x support?
Supported deployment models, platform requirements and component-specific support for 11.x remain
unconfirmed here.
Evidence to watch: Version-specific system requirements and an official deployment/support statement.
How will existing deployments reach 11.x?
No 10.x-to-11.x upgrade edge, in-place conversion or data-movement procedure is published in this guide.
Evidence to watch: READ THIS FIRST, an exact upgrade-path table, migration procedure and rollback limits.
Which premium products, apps and forwarders will pair?
Existing 10.x support does not establish 11.x support for ES, ITSI, SOAR, apps, forwarders or receiver
topologies.
Evidence to watch: Exact app, runtime, premium-product and forwarder/receiver matrices.
What changes for support, security and lifecycle?
No 11.x support deadline, runtime floor, FIPS status or security baseline is inferred from adjacent releases.
